neighbours.label: the determiner after 'on' in on + possessive or definite phrases: on their own, on my feet, on the wrong day; the + pole is 'on a … basis'
fire: After the divorce she was left on her own with two kids.
It took me months to get back on my feet.
We arrived on the wrong platform and missed the train.
The company now finds itself on the back foot in Asia.
All the students were on their best behaviour that day.
He came to London all on his lonesome at twenty.
Our family was back on the road by sunrise.
Most of the workers were on their way home by then.
quiet: After the divorce she saw a counsellor on a weekly basis.
It took me months to pay them on a regular basis.
We check the platforms on a daily basis and report delays.
The company now reports earnings on a per share basis.
All the students were tested on a voluntary basis that day.
He came to London on a monthly basis for work.
Our family was paid on a case by case basis.
Most of the workers were hired on a temporary basis by then.
